text.p: German chemicals and consumer products group Henkel KGaA, posting a six percent rise in nine-month profits, said on Tuesday its key acquisition focus remained on U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp.
Henkel reported a jump in pre-tax profits to 550 million marks ($368 million) for the first nine months on a 15 percent sales rise to 12.1 billion marks on a year ago.
The firm expected the same increase in full year sales to 16 billion marks, compared with 14.2 billion last year, chief executive Hans-Dietrich Winkhaus told a news conference.
Henkel, best known for its Persil washing powder said pre-tax profit was seen growing six percent and net profit five percent in 1996.
"Henkel is on course for solid growth," Winkhaus said, "We are equally positive we will see a good development in 1997."

Highlights of the year were the firm's bid for Loctite, which has not yet agreed to talks, and the recent acquisition of Schwarzkopf haircare products group, which nearly doubled the share of cosmetics in overall turnover.

"We are trying to enter into friendly talks with Loctite to persuade them to support Henkel's offer," Winkhaus said. "We believe such an acquisition we would be strategically very important for the further technological development of the company's adhesives business," he added.

Last week the company said it was launching an offer of $57.75 per share for the 65-percent stake it does not already own in Loctite. Henkel's offer will remain open until January 6 1997, according to an agreement the pair made two years ago.
If Henkel succeeds in merging with Loctite, shareholders' equity was expected to shrink to 30 percent from its current 34.9 percent level, financial director Ulrich Lehner said.
"I do not feel uncomfortable about this," he said, noting the figure should rebound to 35 percent by the year 2,000.
Chief executive Winkhaus said the firm had no plans to integrate Loctite fully into Henkel if the offer was accepted. "It is important to preserve the identity and management of Loctite," he said.
Overall, growth had been stable in Europe, with a slight rise in North America and the main boost from Asia with 45 percent growth, the firm said.
It said domestic sales climbed 12 percent and foreign business increased 18 percent over the year-ago period.
Investments in the first nine months were 352 million marks.
Sales of cosmetics and bodycare products saw the biggest overall jump, at 16.4 percent, to a record 1.986 billion marks, due to the acquisition of Schwarzkopf, the firm said.
Adhesive sales were 16 percent higher at 1.878 billion marks, while chemical products rose three percent to 3.148 billion despite a slump in the domestic market.
Cleaning products rose six percent to 3.17 billion marks, mainly due to strong growth in Russia, China and Egypt said

Henkel said its 280 million mark takeover of U.S. Novamax Technologies would further strengthen its metal chemicals business. In this division Henkel reported a nine percent rise in sales to 762 million marks.
The Duesseldorf-based firm said it chose to announce its results in Vienna to emphasise the international nature of its business and its expansion into Central and Eastern Europe.
